item.title: Every Song That Topped the UK Chart for 8 or More Weeks, But Didn’t Make the Top 10 on the Hot 100
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: "Hey there, music fans. Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest chart-topping hits. I've got some exciting news to share with you today. 'Rein Me In' by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean has reclaimed the top spot on the UK's Official Singles Chart, marking its ninth non-consecutive week at number one. But what's really interesting is that this song is performing differently across the pond."
[Soft music transition]
Host: "In the US, 'Rein Me In' has climbed to number 66 on the Billboard Hot 100, but it's still shy of its peak at number 64. This got us thinking - how often do songs dominate the UK charts without making a splash in the US? It turns out that 'Rein Me In' is one of just five singles to log nine or more weeks at number one in the UK without reaching the top 10 on the Hot 100."
[Upbeat music kicks in]
Host: "But it's not all about the differences. There are songs that have achieved massive success on both sides of the Atlantic. Six songs have reached 10 or more weeks at number one on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the UK's Official Singles Chart. You might recognize some of these hits - Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You', Drake's 'One Dance', and Harry Styles' 'As It Was', to name a few."
[Music transitions to a softer tone]
Host: "It's fascinating to see how music fans in the US and UK can have different tastes, but also come together to celebrate the biggest hits. We'll be keeping an eye on 'Rein Me In' to see if it breaks through in the US, but for now, it's enjoying its time at the top of the UK charts."
[Closing music starts playing]
Host: "That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next episode." [Music fades out]
